title: Fingerprinting the Dispatchers behind Distributed Model Extraction
abstract: arXiv:2611.06661v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: API distillation campaigns try to hide model-stealing traffic by splitting requests across thousands of load-balanced accounts, which standard content classifiers often miss. However, request timestamps, specifically arrival time and stream completion time, reveal the underlying dispatching strategy, such as round-robin counters or key-shuffling pools. Using a 20 percent seed set, this timing analysis can forensically rank the remaining accounts of a campaign with 0.92 to 1.00 AUC within 20 minutes, even across thousands of real production accounts. While adaptive attackers struggle to hide rotating dispatchers using jitter, pinning keys successfully evades detection, though it can severely throttle throughput when quotas bind. Ultimately, timing exposes shared infrastructure patterns even when content filters fail.

translated_title: 指纹识别分布式模型提取背后的调度器
translated_abstract: API蒸馏活动试图通过将请求分散到数千个负载均衡的账户中来隐藏模型窃取流量，而标准内容分类器往往无法检测到这种行为。然而，请求时间戳，特别是到达时间和流完成时间，会暴露底层的调度策略，例如轮询计数器或密钥混洗池。使用20%的种子集，这种时序分析可以在20分钟内以0.92至1.00的AUC对活动中剩余的账户进行取证式排序，即使面对数千个真实生产账户也是如此。虽然自适应攻击者难以通过抖动来隐藏轮换调度器，但固定密钥能够成功规避检测，尽管在配额受限时会严重限制吞吐量。最终，即使在内容过滤器失效的情况下，时序分析也能暴露共享基础设施模式。
tldr: 该论文提出通过请求时间戳（到达时间和流完成时间）指纹识别分布式模型提取攻击背后的调度策略，仅用20%种子集即可在20分钟内以0.92至1.00的AUC对攻击活动中剩余账户进行取证式排序，即使内容分类器失效时也能有效检测此类攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes fingerprinting the dispatching strategies behind distributed model extraction attacks through request timestamps (arrival and stream completion times), enabling forensic ranking of remaining campaign accounts with 0.92-1.00 AUC within 20 minutes using only a 20% seed set, even when content classifiers fail to detect such attacks.
